Usage: [command] [-h|--help] [--version]

Commands:
  alloc         Rank allocation hotspots by bytes; the shortcut for 'rank --metric alloc'.
  callers       Report the immediate callers of a frame; the drill-down after 'rank' finds a hot frame.
  classify      Summarize CPU self-time by runtime work category - zeroing, copying, GC,
      write-barrier, JIT, or other - answering "where did the time go: zeroing memory?
      copying strings? in the GC?". Pair with --native-symbols so the native runtime
      work resolves; without it the native leaves fall in 'other'.
  clean         Remove the ETLX conversion cache beside a trace to force a rebuild on next read.
  collect       Record a Windows ETW (.etl) trace of a launched executable, then print the analysis
      commands the capture unlocks. Windows-only and requires Administrator; for an
      EventPipe (.nettrace) capture use dotnet-trace (cross-platform).
  convert       Build the ETLX conversion cache up front so the first analysis query is fast.
  cpu           Rank CPU-time hotspots; the shortcut for 'rank --metric cpu'.
  diff          Compare two traces and report what got slower or faster between them.
  diskio        Report physical disk I/O by file: bytes read and written to each file, and disk service time.
  events        Query the trace's raw events by name, with paging and a per-event payload cap.
  exceptions    Rank exceptions by type (throw sites via callers) by count; the shortcut for 'rank --metric exceptions'.
  export        Export a trace to a flame-graph file for speedscope or chrome://tracing.
  gcstats       Report garbage-collection behavior: counts by generation, pause-time summary, and per-collection detail.
  heatmap       Build a per-line heat map for a source file.
  info          Report a trace's identity and quality signals - the orientation step to run first.
  jitstats      Report just-in-time compilation: method count, compile-time summary, and per-method detail.
  lines         Rank the hottest source lines of the scoped

Usage: classify [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Summarize CPU self-time by runtime work category - zeroing, copying, GC,
      write-barrier, JIT, or other - answering "where did the time go: zeroing memory?
      copying strings? in the GC?". Pair with --native-symbols so the native runtime
      work resolves; without it the native leaves fall in 'other'.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Path to a .speedscope.json, .nettrace, or .etl file.

Options:
  --root <string>            Substring scoping the classification to the subtree under a frame. [Default: @""]
  -s, --symbols <string?>    Build-output directory whose embedded PDBs resolve managed frames. [Default: null]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]
  --strict                   Exit 3 when symbol resolution is below the trusted threshold.
  --process <string>         Scope to the process tree whose name contains this; omit to auto-scope to the busiest. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process instead of auto-scoping to the busiest (multi-process captures).
  --benchmark                Scope to the BenchmarkDotNet measured-workload subtree (preset root); for BDN captures.
  --native-symbols           Resolve native runtime frames (GC, JIT, memset/memcpy) from the Microsoft public symbol server; opt-in, fetches over the network. .etl captures only.
  --symbol-cache <string>    Local cache directory for downloaded native PDBs; omit for the default under the temp path. [Default: @""]

result.stdout:
Usage: collect [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Record a Windows ETW (.etl) trace of a launched executable, then print the analysis
      commands the capture unlocks. Windows-only and requires Administrator; for an
      EventPipe (.nettrace) capture use dotnet-trace (cross-platform).

Options:
  --launch <string>         Path to the executable to launch and trace (the built app, never 'dotnet run'). [Required]
  --output <string>         Path of the .etl file to write. [Required]
  --metric <string>         What to tune the capture for: cpu (default) or threadtime (adds context switches for wall-clock time). [Default: @"cpu"]
  --launch-args <string>    Arguments passed to the launched executable, as one command-line string. [Default: @""]
  --cpu-ms <double>         CPU sample interval in milliseconds. [Default: 1]
  --duration <int>          Optional cap on capture length in seconds; 0 (default) captures until the process exits. [Default: 0]
  --max-size-mb <int>       Optional cap on the capture's on-disk size in megabytes; 0 (default) writes an unbounded file. When set, a circular buffer keeps the last N MB - size it to hold the run, since a full ring overwrites the oldest events and can drop early JIT method names. [Default: 0]

Usage: cpu [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Rank CPU-time hotspots; the shortcut for 'rank --metric cpu'.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Path to a .speedscope.json, .nettrace, or .etl file.

Options:
  -m, --measure <Measure>    Which measure to report: self (leaf time, helpers folded) or inclusive. Each
      sample weighs 1 ms, so the weights are approximate; the relative percentages are
      exact. [Default: Self]
  --root <string>            Substring scoping the ranking to the subtree under a frame. [Default: @""]
  -n, --top <int>            Maximum number of rows to return. [Default: 25]
  --fold <string[]?>         Extra leaf-frame fold regexes (comma-separated); omit to use the built-in defaults. [Default: null]
  -s, --symbols <string?>    Build-output directory whose embedded PDBs resolve managed frames. [Default: null]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]
  --strict                   Exit 3 when symbol resolution is below the trusted threshold.
  --process <string>         Scope to the process tree whose name contains this; omit to auto-scope to the busiest. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process instead of auto-scoping to the busiest (multi-process captures).
  --benchmark                Scope to the BenchmarkDotNet measured-workload subtree (preset root); for BDN captures.
  --native-symbols           Resolve native runtime frames (GC, JIT, memset/memcpy) from the Microsoft public symbol server; opt-in, fetches over the network. .etl CPU captures only.
  --symbol-cache <string>    Local cache directory for downloaded native PDBs; omit for the default under the temp path. [Default: @""]
  --no-fold                  Fold only the synthetic sample markers, not the JIT-helper thunks, so native runtime leaves rank on their own. Mutually exclusive with --fold.

Usage: rank [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Rank the hottest frames in a trace by self- or inclusive-time.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Path to a .speedscope.json, .nettrace, or .etl file.

Options:
  --metric <string>          Provider metric to rank: cpu (default), alloc, exceptions, threadtime,
      contention, wait, or activity. The cpu metric weights each sample as 1 ms, so its weights
      are approximate; the relative percentages are exact. [Default: @"cpu"]
  -m, --measure <Measure>    Which measure to report: self (leaf time, helpers folded) or inclusive. [Default: Self]
  --root <string>            Substring scoping the ranking to the subtree under a frame. [Default: @""]
  -n, --top <int>            Maximum number of rows to return. [Default: 25]
  --fold <string[]?>         Extra leaf-frame fold regexes (comma-separated); omit to use the built-in defaults. [Default: null]
  -s, --symbols <string?>    Build-output directory whose embedded PDBs resolve managed frames. [Default: null]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]
  --strict                   Exit 3 when symbol resolution is below the trusted threshold.
  --process <string>         Scope to the process tree whose name contains this; omit to auto-scope to the busiest. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process instead of auto-scoping to the busiest (multi-process captures).
  --activity <string>        Scope the ranking to one start-stop activity by task name - the CPU samples taken inside that request/job (cpu metric only); omit for the whole trace. [Default: @""]
  --time <string>            Scope to a time window 'start,end' in ms relative to the trace start; either bound may be omitted (e.g. 1000,5000 or 1000, or ,5000). Applies to every metric. [Default: @""]
  --benchmark                Scope to the BenchmarkDotNet measured-workload subtree (preset root); for BDN captures.
  --native-symbols           Resolve native runtime frames (GC, JIT, memset/memcpy) from th
